descs.t: Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican candidate for Ohio governor, joined Donald Trump on stage at a rally in Chillicothe, Ohio, promising the biggest property tax relief in the state and action by executive order on his first day. Senator Jon Husted also spoke. We walk through what Ramaswamy promised and how the night went.

Donald Trump flew to Chillicothe, Ohio to campaign for Vivek Ramaswamy, who pitched lower property taxes and electric bills, safer streets and better schools, plus a day one executive order. We look at his promises, the crowd's reaction, and whether the rally can move votes in the governor's race.

Vivek Ramaswamy took the stage with Donald Trump in Chillicothe, Ohio and the crowd erupted, with chants of USA through the night. He promised Ohio its biggest property tax relief and action on day one by executive order. Here is the rally, the promises and why Republicans think Ohio is theirs.

intro.plain: Trump was in Chillicothe, Ohio last night campaigning for Vivek Ramaswamy, who is running for governor. Ramaswamy promised the biggest property tax relief in the state and action by executive order on his first day in office. Chat, question for you: what matters most to you in a governor, taxes or something else?
intro.mid: Trump flew to Ohio for one reason: get Vivek Ramaswamy elected governor. Vivek's pitch was simple, lower property taxes and electric bills, safer streets, better schools, and a day one executive order. The crowd loved it. Chat, my question: is a rally like this enough to win a governor's race?
intro.bold: Chillicothe, Ohio was loud last night. Trump brought Vivek Ramaswamy on stage, Vivek promised the biggest property tax cut Ohio has seen and action on his very first day, and the arena chanted USA. Chat, tell me: is Vivek going to win Ohio, and by how much?

hook.plain: Vivek Ramaswamy joined Trump on stage in Ohio with a promise: the biggest property tax relief in the state. Here is what he pledged and how the night went.
hook.mid: Lower taxes, lower bills, and an executive order on day one. That was Vivek Ramaswamy's pitch at Trump's Ohio rally. Here is whether it lands.
hook.bold: The arena erupted the moment Vivek walked out with Trump. Here is the promise that got the biggest cheer, and why Republicans think Ohio is locked.

descs.t: Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy has ordered an investigation into Mary Peltola's Senate campaign over an alleged scheme to put a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot against Senator Dan Sullivan. The move follows New York Times reporting, and reports say the DOJ is also investigating. We walk through what was reported, who is involved and what it means for voters who already cast early ballots.

Mary Peltola calls the same name candidate story a distraction, while Alaska's governor and reportedly the DOJ are now investigating her campaign. Critics say ballot stacking is legal, supporters of Senator Dan Sullivan call it voter fraud. We look at the New York Times report, the role reported for national Democrats and where the Alaska Senate race goes from here.

National Democrats reportedly spent months hunting for another Dan Sullivan to put on Alaska's Senate ballot, and now the governor has ordered a probe. JD Vance says Peltola is trying to steal a Senate seat and Trump wants her prosecuted. We break down the reported scheme, the investigations and why thousands of early votes are now in question.

intro.plain: Alaska's governor has just ordered an investigation into Mary Peltola's Senate campaign. The allegation is that her side recruited a second Dan Sullivan to confuse voters in the race against Senator Dan Sullivan, and reports say the DOJ is looking at it too. Early ballots are already in. So tell me in the chat: should Alaska reprint these ballots?
intro.mid: Mary Peltola calls it a distraction. Alaska's governor calls it serious enough to investigate. The New York Times reported her campaign hunted for a second Dan Sullivan to put on the ballot, and now the DOJ is reportedly involved. Some say ballot stacking is legal. Drop it in the chat: is this a dirty trick or a crime?
intro.bold: This is wild. Democrats reportedly went looking for anyone in Alaska named Dan Sullivan, just to confuse voters against the real Senator Dan Sullivan. Now the governor has ordered a probe, Vance says she is trying to steal a seat, and Trump wants Peltola prosecuted. Thousands already voted. Chat, should Peltola drop out of this race?

hook.plain: Alaska's governor has ordered an investigation into a second Dan Sullivan on the Senate ballot. Here is what was reported, who is involved and what happens next.

hook.bold: They reportedly searched Alaska for anyone named Dan Sullivan to trick voters. Now Peltola's campaign faces a governor's probe and a reported DOJ investigation. Here is how it unravelled.

descs.t: Donald Trump's rally in Chillicothe, Ohio was interrupted by protesters shouting that he went on Jeffrey Epstein's plane, with at least three hauled out in the first few minutes. Trump answered that he threw Epstein out of his club about 20 years ago. We walk through the footage, the hecklers and how Trump responded.

Minutes into Trump's Ohio rally, protesters started yelling about Jeffrey Epstein's plane, one after another, until security removed them. Trump's supporters call them paid protesters; one heckler posted his own footage of being pulled out. We look at what happened, what Trump said back about Epstein, and why the attack line keeps coming.

Heckler after heckler tried to derail Donald Trump's rally in Chillicothe, Ohio with Epstein taunts, and Trump fired back that he threw Jeffrey Epstein out of his club about 20 years ago. Here is the raw footage, the protesters who planned it, and how the crowd and the president handled it.

intro.plain: Trump's rally in Chillicothe, Ohio did not go to plan. Minutes in, protesters started shouting that Trump went on Jeffrey Epstein's plane, and at least three were hauled out. Trump answered that he threw Epstein out of his club about 20 years ago. Chat, what do you make of it: real protest or a stunt?
intro.mid: Five minutes. That is how long Trump's Ohio rally ran before the Epstein hecklers started, one after another, until security pulled them out. Trump's answer: he threw Jeffrey Epstein out of his club about 20 years ago. His fans say these were paid protesters. Chat, my question: does this kind of heckling help or hurt the people doing it?
intro.bold: They came to Trump's rally in Ohio with one line, Epstein's plane, and they used it one after another. Security pulled them out, and Trump hit back that he threw Epstein out of his club about 20 years ago. The crowd did not budge. Chat, be honest: did the hecklers win this one, or did Trump?
